The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No.1118/2021 dated 31.12.2021 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S Rajouri Garden, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Agreement dated 09.08.2023 arrived at between the parties before the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Agreement dated 09.08.2023 [Annexure B] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/12/2023 at 00:31:11 3.
Petitioner nos. 1 to 3 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.

4. Issue Notice.
5.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 12.10.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement Agreement dated 09.08.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.16,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.6,00,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD no. 524143 dated 12.12.2023 issued on RBL Bank Ltd. in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony,
maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She further states that the petitioner no.1 shall additionally transfer to her a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month for a period of 5 years and 6 months w.e.f. 10.08.2023.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In addition to the above, the petitioner no.1 has willingly agreed to deposit a further sum of Rs.5,000/- per month into the account of the child of the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 namely Master Jaskirat Singh [A/c no. 013694100001641, Yes Bank] for the same period of five years and six months as mentioned in the Settlement Agreement.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/12/2023 at 00:31:11 8.

In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

are quashed.

10. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the children of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Jaskirat vis-a-vis his parents,
as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
11.
The petition alongwith the pending application stands disposed of.
